newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 13.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Wednesday:
* The Philippine shares market is likely to consolidate as it seeks a more comfortable support level, brokers said.

* "It's the same thing over and over again. Concerns on the peso situation and its effect on the companies and the economy are causing the selling pressure," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Orion-Squire Capital.
* Traders said that with the Dow's sharp overnight fall, the market is likely to test a support level of 2,500 points.
* On Tuesday, the Philippine composite index closed lower for the fourth straight session, shedding 37.03 points to end at 2,535.40.
* The Dow Jones on Monday ended 101.27 points down at 7,960.84. PLDT's ADR closed lower by $0/12 at $29/13.
* The Philippine peso ended lower at 28.66 to a U.S. dollar versus 28.57.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was steady at 18.0625 percent.
* Philippine banks quoted lower bid and offer rates in the secondary market in reaction to the fall in rates at the auction, traders said.
* The average yields of the 35-day and 42-day treasury bills both fell to 13 percent at the auction, the Bureau of Treasury said.
* The Philippines remained a good buy despite the sharp peso depreciation which left its financial markets badly shaken, separate reports by Merrill Lynch and Bankers Trust said.
* Ayala Corp and its housing and telecommunications subsidiaries have not been affectd by the recent peso depreciation, company officials said.
* SM Prime said it made 1.04 billion pesos for the first six months of the year from 860 million the previous year.
* Globe Telecom said it was raising its 1997 capital expenditure to eight billion pesos from an original 4.7 billion.
* Filinvest Land Inc said it generated 822.6 million in net profits for the first six months of the year from 561.7 the same period last year.
* EEI Corp said it had signed a construction agreement for power plant projects contracted to Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd.

* Philippine Seven Corp said it will push through with its initial public offering involving 71.4 million shares on September 8 to 19 with listing date on the week of Sept 29. The price is seen to range from 6.30 pesos to 7.71.
* Alaska Milk Corp said it has signed an agreement with Nabisco Internal for the distribution of Nabisco biscuits in the Philippines.

* China has pushed back the launch of a Filipino communications satellite by several days from the original blast-off window of August 10-12. The satellite is a project of the Mabuhay Philippines Satellite Corp, a PLDT-led consortium.

* The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) is set to sign a memorandum of agreement setting guidelines for the creation of a small and medium enterprises (SME) trading board, C&P Homes Inc chairman Manuel Villar said.
* The PSE said it had set penalties on members who do not comply with the minimum shareholders requirement and the foreign ownership rule report.
